proposed_action: replace the evaluative appointment claim with the documented presentation and reported hiring
proposed_claim: Lyn Redwood presented on thimerosal at the CDC’s ACIP meeting on June 26, 2025; CBS separately reported that CDC officials said she was being hired for vaccine-safety work.
proposed_title: Lyn Redwood Presented Thimerosal Claims at a CDC Vaccine Advisers Meeting
proposed_short: Lyn Redwood presented on thimerosal at the CDC’s vaccine-advisory meeting on June 26, 2025.
proposed_medium: NBC News reported that Lyn Redwood presented on thimerosal at the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices meeting on June 26, 2025. CNN previewed the planned presentation, and CBS separately reported that CDC officials said Redwood was being hired for vaccine-safety work. The meeting presentation does not establish that her claims were accepted as CDC policy.
proposed_long: On June 26, 2025, Lyn Redwood presented information about thimerosal at a meeting of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices. NBC News reported on the presentation that day and identified Redwood as a former president of Children’s Health Defense. CNN had reported beforehand that she was scheduled to present. CBS News separately reported that CDC officials said the agency was hiring her for vaccine-safety work. These reports support a dated account of the presentation and a separately attributed hiring report. They do not support the original evaluative label “quack,” establish that Robert F. Kennedy Jr. personally appointed her to a formal office, or show that the committee adopted her claims as CDC policy. Her formal job title and the precise terms of any appointment should remain unspecified unless separately documented. CNN described the planned topic as thimerosal in flu vaccines.

source_to_fact_mapping.supports: NBC News reports that Redwood presented on thimerosal at the ACIP meeting on June 26, 2025.
source_to_fact_mapping.access_note: NBC publisher article text returned with the presentation, subject and date.

source_to_fact_mapping.supports: CBS reports that CDC officials said the agency was hiring Redwood for vaccine-safety work.
source_to_fact_mapping.access_note: CBS publisher article text returned; it is used only for the attributed hiring report.

rejected_assertions: A personal RFK Jr. appointment to a formally titled vaccine-safety office.
The presentation established CDC policy or scientific acceptance.
uncertainty: The meeting presentation is directly reported; the hiring is attributed to CBS’s sources, and the formal title/terms are not established here.
